$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {q}_{1} & {q}_{2} & {q}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} & {r}_{13} \\ 0 & {r}_{22} & {r}_{23} \\ 0 & 0 & {r}_{33}\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. You're given that the system of equations given below connects the columns of $Q$ and the columns of $A.$  

$$
{\begin{aligned}{q}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1} \\ {q}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{a}_{2}+{q}_{1} \\ {q}_{3}=\frac{1}{4}{a}_{3}-{q}_{1}+2{q}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

What is the value of ${r}_{11}+{r}_{12}+{r}_{33}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite the vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ as a linear combination of the vectors ${q}_{1},{q}_{2},{q}_{3}:$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{q}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1} \\ {q}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{a}_{2}+{q}_{1} \\ {q}_{3}=\frac{1}{4}{a}_{3}-{q}_{1}+2{q}_{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}=3{q}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}=-2{q}_{1}+2{q}_{2} \\ {a}_{3}=4{q}_{1}-8{q}_{2}+4{q}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, this system can be written in matrix form as follows:

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {q}_{1} & {q}_{2} & {q}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{r}_{11}+{r}_{12}+{r}_{33}=3+(-2)+4=5.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{11}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ 0 & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Finally, ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{11}=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\cdot \sqrt{6}=-2.$

questions.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{22}\cdot {r}_{22}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{9} & \frac{4}{9} & \frac{4}{9} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{9} & 0 \\ \frac{4}{9} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{4}{9} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Finally, ${q}_{22}\cdot {r}_{22}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2}=1.$
